summary.short: Bans data brokers from selling, licensing, transferring or otherwise making available personally identifiable sensitive data of United States individuals to foreign adversary countries or entities they control. The FTC enforces it as an unfair or deceptive practice violation. Effective 60 days after enactment.
summary.long: Division I of Public Law 118-50 prohibits data brokers from selling, licensing, renting, trading, transferring, releasing, disclosing, providing access to or otherwise making available personally identifiable sensitive data of United States individuals to a foreign adversary country or an entity controlled by one. 'Data broker' excludes service providers and some other entities, such as those transmitting data at the individual's direction or publishing news. 'Sensitive data' is a defined list, including government identifiers, health and financial data, biometric and genetic information, precise geolocation, private communications, data on minors under 17 and online activity over time. Foreign adversary countries are those in 10 U.S.C. 4872(d)(2); control includes foreign ownership of at least 20 percent. The Federal Trade Commission enforces the prohibition as a violation of an unfair or deceptive practices rule under FTC Act section 18(a)(1)(B), with that Act's powers and penalties. The prohibition takes effect 60 days after enactment. No AI-specific provisions appear in this excerpt.

notes: Annotates Division I only, as reproduced from Pub. L. 118-50 (pages 961-963 of 138 Stat. shown); Divisions A-H and J-T are omitted in the supplied text. Operative provisions are in Sec. 2; Sec. 1 is the short title. The 15 USC 9901 markers are codification references, not operative text. The addressee is the class 'data broker' (Sec. 2(c)(3)), not a named firm. The division states no penalty amounts; Sec. 2(b)(2)(B) imports FTC Act penalties by reference. The effective date is 60 days after enactment (Sec. 2(d)); the text records approval on April 24, 2024, and the effective date is not computed here. No internal inconsistencies found. Sec. 2(c)(4) and Sec. 2(c)(3)(B)(iv)(II) depend on other laws not included in the text.
